source_name: OneID — Macedonian qualified electronic identification service (KIBS)
why_relevant: KIBS's eIDAS-aligned digital-trust/eID arm; onboarding and relying-party lists indicate which banks and PSPs adopt domestic eID for KYC/onboarding — adjacent tech-supply intelligence to card/switch rails.

source_name: CaSys services page — issuing / acquiring / personalisation / call centre
why_relevant: Most explicit public statement of the processor's capability matrix (chip/contactless/wearable personalisation, clearing file preparation, Mastercard/Visa network connections, e-commerce portal). Baseline for gap analysis against vendor offerings (HSM, tokenisation, issuing platforms).

source_name: NBRNM — Payment systems and payment services section
why_relevant: Regulator's hub for payment-system regulation, oversight decisions and system descriptions; the authoritative place where operators (MIPS, KIBS, CaSys/ICS) and their licensing status are described.

source_name: NBRNM — CaSys / International Card System AD system description page
why_relevant: Regulator's own description of CaSys as a multilateral deferred net settlement system for domestic-brand payment cards — the authoritative statement of the domestic card scheme/settlement arrangement (the closest thing MK has to a national card scheme).

source_name: Macedonian Banking Association (МБА) — e-bulletin and member content
why_relevant: Publishes an e-bulletin carrying interviews with infrastructure operators (KIBS General Director, issue 20, April 2026) and hosts a KIBS tag archive; the association's membership and working groups map the bank-side counterparties of the rails.

source_name: eCommerce4all.mk — e-payment processing module (MK e-commerce association resource)
why_relevant: Neutral explainer of how MK online card processing works and who the acquirers/processors/gateways are — a compact pointer to the acquiring value chain from the merchant side, useful for enumerating gateway options per bank.

source_name: ecommerce.mk — Macedonian E-commerce Association news (CaSys product launches)
why_relevant: Association news channel carrying CaSys product announcements (new payment products, virtual cards); shows product roadmap and merchant-side adoption signals for the domestic processor.

source_name: SeeNews — South-East Europe business wire (MK payments deals)
why_relevant: Reliable English wire for MK processor/scheme deals — reported CaSys becoming Diners Club processor and the Diners Club International Mak ownership change from Erste Card Club. Good for dated, citable partnership events.

source_name: Diners Club International Mak (Diners Club Macedonia) — issuer/acquirer of the DC franchise
why_relevant: Holder of the Diners Club franchise in MK (first credit card in the country, 1996; ~3,000 acceptance outlets), locally owned since the 2020 buy-out from Erste Card Club, and a CaSys processing client — a distinct three-party acquiring network beside the bank acquirers.

source_name: AmCham North Macedonia — member directory (CaSys, Asseco SEE, Diners Club)
why_relevant: Business-chamber directory that co-locates payments infrastructure actors and their tech suppliers with short company profiles; useful for snowballing the vendor set around the rails (e.g. Asseco SEE/Payten presence in MK) and for event/partnership signals.

source_name: CompanyWall MK / zk.mk — company registry mirrors for КИБС АД and CaSys АД
why_relevant: Aggregators of Central Register data: legal names, EMBS/EDB identifiers, ownership, management and financial results for KIBS AD and Internacionalen Karticen Sistem AD — reveals shareholder structure (which banks own the rails) and financial scale without a paid registry subscription.

source_name: Payten / Asseco SEE (ASEE) — regional ATM/POS and processing vendor group
why_relevant: The dominant regional supplier group for ATM/POS services, e-commerce, mPayments and processing outsourcing; ASEE has an MK presence (AmCham member). Their reference/news pages are a key route to identifying which MK banks or the processor use their switching/terminal estate.

source_name: Wikipedia (mk) — Македонски Интербанкарски Платен Систем
why_relevant: Low-credibility but high-yield pointer: consolidates MIPS history, participant categories, SWIFT-standard operation and cut-off times, with citations back to NBRNM — a fast orientation and citation-harvesting layer when nbrm.mk blocks automated access.

source_name: Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems (ЗПУПС) — consolidated text (NBRNM PDF)
why_relevant: Defines the licensing regime for payment system operators, PIs and EMIs, the statutory registers, and the obligations (incl. instant payments) that drive infrastructure procurement — the legal backbone explaining why KIBS obtained an instant-payments operator licence in 2025.

source_name: Printec Group — Printec North Macedonia country page & customer stories
why_relevant: Printec's MK country page describes its local footprint since 2006 and names financial-institution engagements (e.g. HALKBANK AD Skopje multifunction NCR SelfServ ATMs with cash deposit/recycling). Vendor-published, named-customer evidence for ATM/self-service competitor mapping.

source_name: Nextsense — banking news / customer announcements (Komercijalna Banka digital onboarding platform)
why_relevant: Skopje-headquartered vendor publishing a named win at Komercijalna Banka AD Skopje (remote account opening, e-banking activation, debit card issuance). Direct evidence of who supplies MK digital-channel/onboarding stacks.

source_name: Entrust — press release: card digitization / push provisioning to Google Pay for Komercijalna Banka AD Skopje
why_relevant: Named MK bank win by a global issuance/tokenization vendor (Entrust issuer TSP hub + Digital Card Solution SDK inside the mBanka app). Shows which international card-tech vendors already sell into MK.

source_name: Apps Run The World — customer technographics profile: Stopanska Banka (North Macedonia)
why_relevant: Third-party technographics aggregator that names the vendor stack per MK institution (e.g. Temenos T24 core, Oracle Mantas AML, Microsoft Azure/365 with adoption years). Fast triangulation of vendor-bank pairs that vendors themselves never publish.

source_name: ASEE / Asseco South Eastern Europe — corporate site (ASEE Macedonia, Skopje)
why_relevant: ASEE runs a Skopje entity (Naroden Front 17) and is a top SEE banking-software and payments player; its solutions/references/news pages are the natural place named MK bank deployments (core, e/m-banking, ATM/POS) surface.

source_name: Payten (ASEE group) — payments solutions & references site
why_relevant: ASEE's payments arm covering acquiring/processing, ATM and POS services across SEE; the operating vehicle most likely holding MK bank card/POS contracts. Its offer and reference pages are the pointer to named MK wins.

source_name: CaSys — Интернационален Картичен Систем АД Скопје (card processor) news & partner announcements
why_relevant: MK's independent Visa/Mastercard-certified processor; publishes bank and merchant partnership announcements (e.g. cooperation with Albanian fintech Rubicon on chip personalisation, virtual cards, e-commerce, ATM network management). Reveals who processes for which MK bank and which sub-vendors sit behind it.

source_name: G+D Netcetera — Knowledge Hub / customer stories (Skopje & Ohrid delivery centres)
why_relevant: Major digital-banking and 3DS/ACS vendor with substantial MK engineering presence (Skopje, Ohrid); its stories/case-study hub is where named bank and PSP customers appear, including regional ones relevant to MK issuers.

source_name: Google Play / App Store listings for MK bank apps (developer & package-ID attribution)
why_relevant: App package IDs and developer fields silently reveal the white-label vendor behind a bank's channel — e.g. Halkbank Skopje's app ships under 'eu.newfrontier.iBanking...', pointing at a third-party mobile-banking platform rather than in-house build. Cheap, high-signal vendor attribution across every MK bank.

source_name: Thales CPL partner directory — NEXTSENSE D.O.O. partner profile
why_relevant: Vendor partner directories expose the supply chain behind MK deployments (here: Thales cryptography/HSM/identity delivered through a Skopje integrator). Partner-locator pages are a reliable, under-used pointer to who implements what locally.

source_name: Komercijalna Banka AD Skopje — investor presentations & press (technology partner disclosures)
why_relevant: Bank-side counterpart to vendor claims: quarterly investor presentations and press releases describe digital-channel launches (mBanka, One ID, digital branch) that can be matched to the vendor announcements naming the same projects.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf newsroom / customer stories
why_relevant: One of the two global ATM/branch-automation OEMs competing for MK bank fleets. No MK-named story surfaced in this pass, but the newsroom is the canonical place such a win would be published and must be monitored.

source_name: NCR Atleos newsroom / customer stories
why_relevant: NCR SelfServ hardware is demonstrably deployed in MK (via Printec at Halkbank), so NCR Atleos' own newsroom and case-study library is a second, OEM-level channel for MK deployment evidence and for spotting channel-partner structure.
